London, 24<sup>th</sup> April 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**General Motors** appears to be firmly fixing its sights on the bankruptcy courts after its chief financial officer admitted it intends to default on a $1bn (£690m) bond debt payment due in June.  GM now faces an almost certain Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing unless it can persuade holders of $28bn of its unsecured bonds to swap them for equity.  The non-payment of the $1bn is unlikely to swing bondholders in GM’s favour, however, and is set to be viewed as a negotiating tactic by creditors who will play a vital role in ensuring whether the company can restructure its $62bn debt pile by the US government’s June 1. 

GM’s CFO Ray Young admitted that the company doesn’t intend to make the $1bn due on June 1, confessing that GM is relying on either a successful debt-for-equity swap or the bankruptcy courts to lower its debts. GM will launch the debt-for-equity exchange in the coming days – as bondholders must be given a whole month to decide whether to accept it or not. However, Young admitted that a trip to the bankruptcy courts is “probable”. It is not known whether bondholders will support the debt exchange, but it should be noted that Chrysler creditors recently rejected plans to reduce borrowings by 85pc in favour of a revised plan reducing debts by just 35pc.   GM has also been discussing the possibility of exchanging $10bn owed to the United Auto Workers union for the establishment of a retired workers health care trust for new shares, but those talks have stalled as the UAW focuses on its talks with Chrysler. _Source:  The Telegraph_ 

**Chrysler** is ever closer to bankruptcy, The Wall Street Journal, BusinessWeek and New York Times reported.  It could file for Chapter 11 as early as next week regardless of whether or not it cinches a deal with Fiat and/or its demanding bondholders. An auto industry analyst said a Chrylser bankruptcy is a “95% likelihood.” _Source:  Reuters_ 

**Lonmin’s** refined pgm production increased by 45% y-o-y to 362,326 oz in Q1 09.  Platinum production rose by 41% to 185,284 oz, mainly as a result of an improvement from underground operations at Marikana.  Production of saleable platinum rose by 30% to 185,561 oz in Q1 09; saleable pgm output was up 26% to 355,069 oz. 

_Source:  Lonmin_ 

**Braemore Resources’** Mintek smelter produced 10,574 PGM oz in Q1 09.  The smelter, which suffered damage to its furnace on March 27, was fully repaired and in operation since April 17. _Source:  Interactive Investor_ 

**AU Optronics** is optimistic about the current panel industry and will increase 2009 capex to NT$50-60 billion (US$1.48-1.78 billion) from previous estimation of NT$50 billion, as it decided to bring forward volume production at its 8.5G plant to the end of Q2 09.  Initial production of AUO’s 8.5G plant will concentrate on 46-, 52-, and 55-inch panels with monthly capacity of 10,000 substrates, and the company estimates its capacity wil

l reach 20,000 substrates in September.  As the global LCD TV market is estimated to reach 120-125 million units with China accounting for over 20 million units in 2009, AUO’s TV panel shipments to China are estimated to increase by 20-30% this year.  For LCD monitor panels, AUO is optimistic regarding the 16:9 aspect ratio and larger-size segments. It estimates that the mainstream will shift to 21.5-inch and 24-inch full HD widescreen this year from 19-inch widescreen in 2008.  AUO expects its utilization to be almost full in Q209, compared to 65% in Q109.  Utilization of 6G and above production lines for large-size panels will reach almost 100% in Q2 09, while utilization of 5G and lower production lines for small- to medium-size panels will be lower, as market demand for small- to medium-size panels will be relatively weaker. _Source:  Digtimes_
